captions.Fig2: Analytically established acquisition regimes on diagonal bands. Each separate column represents one integer archive length N; no values between columns are implied. The completion width satisfies 0<d<=1. For K=3, the zero-overhead and first-supercritical regions include their upper boundaries and hold for arbitrary fixed positive row prices and nonnegative common setup. The marked five-row triangular case has unit-price, zero-setup ratios 71/67 and 15/14. For K>=3 at unit prices and zero setup, 0<dN<=1 gives the exact unbounded-domain formula; outside this range the general comparison provides bounds. At d=0 the positive class is empty and no acquisition ratio is assigned.
captions.Fig3: A fixed alphabet and the cost of requiring complete candidate observation. (A) The raw symbols are (0,0), (1,0) and (1,1). The displayed mean vectors of the two hard worlds use N=12 and q=3. Diamonds and squares mark candidates, coloured circles mark left rivals, and the shared right rival is (1,0); the two lines join the rivals. (B) Lower and upper bounds for accumulation points of the optimal acquisition ratios as integer N grows, on the continuous triangle with K=3, unit row prices and zero setup. The middle row restricts policies to full candidate observation before TRUE on every positive archive; its interval has width 3/8800. These are theorem bounds, not confidence intervals or measured performance. Convergence and the exact unrestricted asymptotic constants remain open.
